info.name: QX Broker — HTTP Admin API
info.description:
# QX Broker — HTTP Admin API

qx (queuex) is a Rust message broker that speaks two primary data-plane protocols: **gRPC** (its native client API) and the **Kafka wire protocol**. Those two protocols carry all produce/consume/transaction/consumer-group traffic and are explicitly NOT covered by this collection.

This collection maps ONLY the broker's HTTP surface, which is a small, **read-only introspection/observability** layer. All HTTP routes are served by a single custom HTTP/1.1 listener (`handle_metrics_connection` in `crates/broker/src/server.rs`) that multiplexes three things on one port: the Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, a JSON dashboard-data API under `/api/*` (consumed by the embedded qx-dashboard SPA — see `crates/broker/src/admin_api.rs`), and the embedded dashboard static assets / SPA shell. The listener defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:9090` and is configured via the `[metrics].addr` block in `qx.toml` (set `[metrics].addr = "off"` to disable the HTTP surface entirely).

**Auth:** the HTTP surface is entirely UNAUTHENTICATED and public. The broker's bearer-token / keyx (`crates/broker/src/auth_keyx.rs`, admin/owner role) authentication applies ONLY to the gRPC listener via `check_auth_combined`, which returns gRPC `Status` codes — it is never invoked on the HTTP path. Every HTTP response is emitted with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so the Vite dev dashboard (:5173) can fetch cross-origin. Only `GET` (and CORS-preflight `OPTIONS`) are handled; any other path returns `404 Not Found` with the plain-text body `not found\n` (there is NO JSON error envelope on the HTTP surface).

**Response shape:** raw JSON, unwrapped. `/api/health` returns a single object; `/api/nodes`, `/api/topics`, `/api/groups`, `/api/workflows`, `/api/events` each return a bare JSON array. `/metrics` returns Prometheus text exposition (`text/plain; version=0.0.4`).

UNCERTAINTIES: (1) No production HTTP host is defined anywhere in the repo (the broker has no production deployments per docs/COMPARISON.md); the stage hostnames below follow the assumed `admin.qx.vexarr.com` vexarr convention and are PLACEHOLDERS — in practice qx is reached at its local/cluster bind address. (2) The default port 9090 collides with Prometheus's own default; operators are expected to override `[metrics].addr`.

## Authentication

The HTTP surface (/metrics, /api/*, dashboard assets) is fully PUBLIC and unauthenticated — there is no Authorization check in handle_metrics_connection. The broker's bearer-token + keyx validation (admin/owner role, crates/broker/src/auth_keyx.rs) is enforced ONLY on the gRPC data-plane listener (check_auth_combined), not on HTTP. An access_token variable is kept in the collection only in case a reverse proxy is placed in front of the broker to add auth; the broker itself ignores it.


## Stages

One collection serves every stage — switch the Postman *environment* to switch stage.

| Stage | `base_url` |
| --- | --- |
| Local / Dev | `http://localhost:9090` |
| Integration | `https://admin.integration.qx.vexarr.com` |
| Staging | `https://admin.staging.qx.vexarr.com` |
| Production | `https://admin.qx.vexarr.com` |

## Examples & tests

Every request ships ≥ 5 saved example responses (one per status case) and a `test` script that asserts the response shape, the success payload's fields, and captures ids/tokens into collection variables for chaining. A collection-level test runs baseline assertions on every request.

> Generated from `_inventory.json` by `gen_collection.py`.

request.description:
**Broker health / liveness**

Liveness probe. Returns broker status and uptime in seconds. No auth; public. Raw JSON object (NOT an array).

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /api/health`

response.name: 405 — Method Not Allowed (METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
response.body: HTTP method not allowed for this route.

exec: pm.test('Status code is one of the documented codes', function () {
if (isJson) { pm.test('Body parses as JSON', function () { json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.be.an('object'); }); }
if (json.status !== undefined && json.status !== null) { pm.collectionVariables.set('status', String(json.status)); }

request.description:
**Prometheus metrics (text exposition)**

Prometheus scrape endpoint. Content-Type text/plain; version=0.0.4. Emits per-topic gauges: qx_topic_pending, qx_topic_inflight, qx_topic_dead, qx_topic_partitions (each labelled {topic=...}). Public, no auth. NOT JSON — set Accept to text/plain. If the broker is built without an embedded dashboard, GET / also serves this same metrics text (legacy 'Prometheus at root' behaviour).

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /metrics`

response.name: 200 — OK
response.body:
# HELP qx_topic_pending Messages awaiting delivery.
# TYPE qx_topic_pending gauge
qx_topic_pending{topic="orders"} 42
# HELP qx_topic_inflight Messages claimed by a consumer, not yet acked.
# TYPE qx_topic_inflight gauge
qx_topic_inflight{topic="orders"} 7
# HELP qx_topic_dead Messages in the dead-letter state.
# TYPE qx_topic_dead gauge
qx_topic_dead{topic="orders"} 0
# HELP qx_topic_partitions Configured partition count.
# TYPE qx_topic_partitions gauge
qx_topic_partitions{topic="orders"} 6

response.name: 405 — Method Not Allowed (METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
response.body: HTTP method not allowed for this route.

request.description:
**Cluster nodes / Raft peers**

Returns one row per broker node: the local node plus every configured Raft peer. Each row carries live openraft state (term, commitIndex, lastApplied), role (leader/follower/candidate), status, and uptimeSeconds. In single-node mode returns just the local node. Raw JSON array.

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /api/nodes`

response.name: 405 — Method Not Allowed (METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
response.body: HTTP method not allowed for this route.

exec: pm.test('Status code is one of the documented codes', function () {
if (isJson) { pm.test('Body parses as JSON', function () { json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.be.an('object'); }); }
pm.test('payload is an array', function () { pm.expect(json).to.be.an('array'); });
if (json.id !== undefined && json.id !== null) { pm.collectionVariables.set('node_id', String(json.id)); }

request.description:
**Topics with live stats & rates**

Returns one row per open topic with real pending/inflight/dead counts (from a ~1s-stale background cache to avoid locking partition mutexes) plus live per-second message and byte rates computed as deltas between successive polls (first poll returns 0.0). Raw JSON array.

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /api/topics`

response.name: 405 — Method Not Allowed (METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
response.body: HTTP method not allowed for this route.

exec: pm.test('Status code is one of the documented codes', function () {
if (isJson) { pm.test('Body parses as JSON', function () { json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.be.an('object'); }); }
pm.test('payload is an array', function () { pm.expect(json).to.be.an('array'); });
if (json.name !== undefined && json.name !== null) { pm.collectionVariables.set('topic', String(json.name)); }

request.description:
**Consumer groups (gRPC + Kafka) with lag**

Returns one row per (group, topic) combining gRPC-side consumer groups and Kafka coordinator groups. Kafka rows carry real per-(group,topic) lag joined against each partition's high-water mark; gRPC rows report lag 0 (their pending lives in /api/topics 'pending'). status is one of empty/stable/rebalancing. Raw JSON array.

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /api/groups`

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

request.description:
**Recent broker event log**

Returns recent broker events from a bounded in-memory ring buffer (info/warn/error severities, monotonic ids for de-dup across overlapping polls). Note: in the current build this is largely a placeholder and is frequently an empty array. Raw JSON array.

_Public endpoint — no auth required._

`GET /api/events`

response.name: 405 — Method Not Allowed (METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
response.body: HTTP method not allowed for this route.

exec: pm.test('Status code is one of the documented codes', function () {
if (isJson) { pm.test('Body parses as JSON', function () { json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.be.an('object'); }); }
pm.test('payload is an array', function () { pm.expect(json).to.be.an('array'); });
pm.test('Body parses as JSON', function () { body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.not.be.undefined; });
